---
title: "About this site"
---

We are a group of dedicated *teachers* specializing in digital system design at the [Microelectronics Laboratory](https://www.up-microlab.org/) of the [Electrical and Electronics Engineering Institute (EEEI)](https://eee.upd.edu.ph/) at the [University of the Philippines Diliman](https://upd.edu.ph/). Through **digital.eee**, we bring together crash courses, exercises, and interactive simulators to help students understand digital design, from fundamental concepts to complex compute architectures. We emphasize intuitive visuals and generous, step-by-step guidance so students can explore how things work at their own pace.

As the collection grows, we hope to share the breadth and depth of the institute’s teaching with students and educators at other universities, not just locally but also internationally. **Our aim is to democratize digital design education by making these resources accessible to anyone who wants to learn.**

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" icon="false" title="Short history (from the main author)"}

**digital.eee** began with the [Verilog Crash Course](https://digital.eee.upd.edu.ph/pages/verilogCrashCourse/index.html), which I wrote to address an appalling shortage of competent digital system designers in the institute. When I returned from my PhD studies abroad in mid-2023, I could rely on only three people in the lab to design digital systems competently. All three were lecturers nearing the end of their graduate degrees. Once they graduated, I would be the only designer left in the lab with recent hands-on experience in large-scale, system-level design. Research on more complex architectures depended on developing people who could carry it forward, starting with strong fundamentals. I wrote the crash course to help build that foundation and first distributed it through [UVLe](https://uvle.upd.edu.ph/), the university’s online learning management system, in mid-2025.

Even then, I imagined a broader collection that students could return to as they progressed from the fundamentals to the advanced topics I care about. I also wanted students and educators at other universities to see what we teach and study, and to have resources they could adapt alongside their own approaches. My wish was for students, wherever they study, to have the opportunity to build equally strong foundations in digital design.

The collection began to take shape when Lawrence created [Vercises](https://digital.eee.upd.edu.ph/exercises) to hold the crash course’s companion exercises. He also coined the name, short for "Verilog Exercises." We then expanded the idea into the [Verilog IDE](https://digital.eee.upd.edu.ph/verilog), where students could write and simulate any Verilog code. We decided to bring both tools and the crash course together on one website, choosing the domain name **digital.eee.upd.edu.ph** on September 16, 2025. Lawrence designed and implemented the hosting infrastructure in late 2025, giving the growing collection a shared home.

Interactive simulators became the next step. I had grown frustrated with relying on slide animations and doodles to explain fundamental concepts that students could understand more easily by seeing them in action. I find it quite disappointing that there are no available online tools that visualized them quite as I wanted to teach them. In early 2026, Isaac’s work on [FSM_simulatEEE](https://digital.eee.upd.edu.ph/FSM_simulatEEE.html) and [ASM_simulatEEE](https://digital.eee.upd.edu.ph/ASM_simulatEEE.html) for the digital design fundamentals course showed me a way forward. Seeing how much he could do in a single, self-contained HTML file inspired me to build similarly engaging simulators for the other courses I teach and share them here.

Looking ahead, I hope students will use these resources to design systems of their own, pursue new research questions, and bring what they learn into their classrooms and communities. It would mean a great deal to me to see today’s learners become the designers, researchers, and teachers who help the next generation get started.

*—Adelson Chua*

:::

## Contributors

The people behind digital.eee are:

<!-- To add a portrait, save the photo under pages/images/team/ and uncomment the matching image below. -->

**Adelson Chua — Main content contributor**

I develop most of the site’s content and shape its educational direction. The materials and simulators reflect my taste in teaching: intuitive, highly visual, and deliberately generous with guidance. I want students to follow what happens, explore why it happens, and work through the details at their own pace.
